messages.subject: Genetic Mapping: Deleting Duplicate Markers
parts:
Hi Karl,

I am working with a relatively large dataset. It is a "riself" population of 65 individuals with ~7500 markers. The genotypes % for AA and BB are 48.8 and 51.2 respectively. I am working through your genetic mapping article and want to remove the identical markers; however, when the identical markers are removed, the marker count drops to <50. This seems rather extreme in my opinion. I was expecting to have ~1000 markers remaining. Is there a possibility of something else going wrong besides having poor marker data/identical markers? I will also note that some markers are SNPs and others are indels as well.

my code is as follows:
print(dup<-findDupMarkers(map, exact.only=FALSE))
#the above lists over 7000 markers that are exact

I am attaching a "dummy.version" of my file for you as well. 

Best,
Sarah

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Genetic Mapping: Deleting Duplicate Markers
parts:
There do seem to be a large number of effectively duplicate markers, but when I drop the duplicates, I still have 1841 markers left.

library(qtl)
x <- read.cross("csv", file="dummy.map.csv", genotypes=c("A", "B"), crosstype="riself")
dup <- findDupMarkers(x, exact.only=FALSE)
length(dup) # 1001 groups of duplicated markers
length( unlist(dup) ) # 5727 markers that you might drop

x_reduced <- drop.markers(x, unlist(dup) )

totmar(x) # 7568 markers
totmar(x_reduced) # 1841 markers (= 7568 - 5727)

You could pull out the genotype data and look at a set of these duplicates.

g <- pull.geno(x)
g_dup1 <- g[, c(names(dup)[1], dup[[1]])]
dim(g_dup1) # 65 lines x 32 markers
g_dup1

They do look all the same, though with some having a lot of missing genotypes.

karl

parts:
Hi Karl,

Thank you for the advice so far. Unfortunately after running your code I did not get remotely similar results. When running your code my object dup had 26 markers and the length of the unlisted object dup was 7540. Before identifying duplicate markers, I run the loop in your genetic mapping article for removing duplicate individuals. Before eliminating the duplicate markers the map file has 7566 markers.

#running loop eliminating mismatching genotypes
for(i in 1:nrow(wh)) {
tozero<-!is.na(g[wh[i,1],]) & !is.na(g[wh[i,2],]) &
g[wh[i,1],] != g[wh[i,2],]
map$geno[[1]]$data[wh[i,1],tozero]<-NA
}

#omit one individual for each pair
map<-subset(map, ind = wh[,2])
totmar(map) #returns value of 7566

#looking for duplicate markers
dup<-findDupMarkers(map, exact.only = F)
length(dup) #returns value of 26
length(unlist(dup)) #returns value of 7540

Earlier on I also do more quality control of eliminating Individuals missing many markers and markers missing genotypes. But if through that I narrow my markers down to 7566 markers, I don't see how it still narrows down to 26 markers that aren't duplicates?

Thanks,
Sarah

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Genetic Mapping: Deleting Duplicate Markers
parts: At this step in your script:

you are omitting all but 5 of the individuals

That's the reason that at the next step, the markers look to be largely
duplicates; there are just five individuals left.

I don't think there is overwhelming evidence for duplicate samples, and
so I wouldn't omit any samples. The closest pair has 7% mismatch.

karl
